summary: Sega AM2's landmark polygonal Formula racing game, tracked by arcade, home-port, and Sega Ages remaster routes.

entries.title: Virtua Racing
entries.definitive_edition: SEGA AGES Virtua Racing plus 32X/Saturn/PS2 content supplements

emulation.emulator: Nintendo Switch hardware / Genesis Plus GX for 32X supplement / Mednafen or Beetle Saturn for Saturn / PCSX2 for PS2
emulation.notes: Use Switch for the main arcade run; emulate or use original hardware only for the secondary content branches.

primary.why: The Switch SEGA AGES release is an M2 port of the original arcade game with 60fps, 16:9 presentation, online two-player, local eight-player, leaderboards, replays, easier steering, and a Grand Prix option. It is the highest-fidelity and most practical arcade-original route, while 32X, Saturn, and PS2 are preserved as secondary routes for their exclusive tracks/cars.
primary.how_to_play: Play SEGA AGES Virtua Racing on Nintendo Switch; use the 32X, Saturn, and PS2 versions only to sample their exclusive content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Virtua Racing Deluxe adds Stock and Prototype cars plus Highland and Sand Park tracks.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the two extra tracks and try the two extra cars.
secondary.why: Lower fidelity than Switch, but it has unique content not in the arcade-original SEGA AGES route.

secondary.exclusive_content: VR Virtua Racing adds seven new courses, four new cars, an unlockable F-200 Super Car, and Grand Prix mode.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Saturn-only courses/cars and Grand Prix mode.
secondary.why: The Saturn release is a less faithful conversion but has a large exclusive-content set.

secondary.exclusive_content: Virtua Racing: FlatOut / Sega Classics Collection adds three new courses and four new cars.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PS2 remake's new courses and cars after the Switch main route.
secondary.why: The PS2 remake is not the pure arcade version, but it has unique content.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Sega Model 1 arcade release, including deluxe cabinet variants.
all_releases.reason: skip: authentic baseline, but Switch provides the arcade game at 60fps/16:9 with modern features.
skip: unique cabinet experience, but no sourced content advantage over the Switch route.
skip: historically important but lower fidelity and less complete than later routes.

all_releases.fidelity: Virtua Racing Deluxe, closer to arcade than Genesis and with extra cars/tracks.
Time Warner Interactive's VR Virtua Racing, with many added tracks/cars but less arcade accuracy.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive cars, courses, and Grand Prix mode.

all_releases.fidelity: Virtua Racing: FlatOut / Sega Classics Collection remake with new content.
all_releases.reason: secondary: exclusive PS2 remake courses and cars.

all_releases.fidelity: SEGA AGES arcade port with 60fps, 16:9, online/local multiplayer, leaderboards, replays, and Grand Prix option.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most practical arcade-original route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Switch is the best arcade-original fidelity route; 32X, Saturn, and PS2 each have exclusive tracks/cars that require secondary sampling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Switch is based on the original arcade game and does not replace the unique added content in the 32X, Saturn, or PS2 remake branches.
